atoms.b: Each animal has slightly different teeth depending on what food they eat. ((--// ++ )) They have adapted over long periods of time to be perfect for the animal’s needs. ((++// -- )) Carnivores have particularly long and sharp canines, which tear through meat with ease. ((--// ++ )) They also have carnassials in the back of their mouths to help them chew through the meat. ((++// -- )) However, herbivores do not have any canines. ((--// ++ )) Instead they have incisors which are adapted to cut through vegetation. ((--// ++ )) They also have molars at the back of their mouths to grind down the plant matter.

end.text: Each paragraph indicates a shift in focus. The first paragraph talks about teeth generally, the second paragraph talks about carnivore teeth and the third paragraph talks about herbivore teeth.

instruction.text: Break up the text below into paragraphs. If a new paragraph should be started, add a paragraph marker (//). If no new paragraph should be started, add a space.

atoms.b: Humans have domesticated animals for thousands of years. ((--// ++ )) Instead of living in the wild, the animals live as property of humans in their homes, stables or fields. ((++// -- )) Pets are animals that have been domesticated for companionship. ((--// ++ )) It is thought that wolves were domesticated into pets more than 30,000 years ago. ((--// ++ )) The dogs we own today looks very little like their ancestors. ((++// -- )) Livestock are animals that have been domesticated to produce food and other products for humans. ((--// ++ )) This can include eggs, wool, milk, leather and meat.

end.text: Each paragraph indicates a shift in focus. The first paragraph discusses domesticated animals in general. The second and third paragraphs go into more detail about the types of domesticated animals.
